title: 2016 AMC 10A 25
statement: How many ordered triples \((x,y,z)\) of positive integers satisfy \[\text{lcm}(x,y) = 72,\]\[ \text{lcm}(x,z) = 600,\] and \[\text{lcm}(y,z)=900?\]

solutions.text:
Factor the given least common multiples: \[ \begin{gathered} 72=2^3\cdot3^2, \\ \quad 600=2^3\cdot3\cdot5^2, \\ \quad 900=2^2\cdot3^2\cdot5^2. \end{gathered} \] Since \(\operatorname{lcm}(x,y)\) has no factor of \(5\), neither \(x\) nor \(y\) has a factor of \(5\), and \(z\) must contain \(5^2\).

Write \(x=2^a3^b\), \(y=2^c3^d\), and \(z=2^e3^f5^2\). The power of \(3\) in \(\operatorname{lcm}(y,z)\) forces \(d=2\), and the power of \(2\) in \(\operatorname{lcm}(x,z)\) forces \(a=3\).

The remaining independent conditions are \(\max(b,f)=1\) and \(\max(c,e)=2\). These have \(3\) and \(5\) ordered choices, respectively, so there are \(3\cdot5=15\) triples.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The powers of \(3\) and \(2\) each leave a small max-condition count
